title: Leviticus veiled like the Word in flesh
english: [[Just as in the last days >> Bible:Hebrews 1:2]] the Word of God came forth from Mary clothed in flesh — one thing seen, another understood — so when the Word speaks through the prophets or the lawgiver it wears the veil of the letter. Leviticus’s rites and victims are letter like flesh; the spiritual sense is divinity within. Blessed are the eyes that see the Spirit under that veil. Those who cling to bare history are driven to offer calves and lambs; the church answers with Susanna: [[better to fall into your hands than to sin against the Lord >> Bible:Daniel 13:22-23]]. [[When one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away; where the Spirit of the Lord is, there is freedom >> Bible:2 Corinthians 3:16-17]]. [[Open my eyes, and I will behold wonders from your law >> Bible:Psalm 119:18]].

title: The Lord called Moses — beginning of Leviticus
english: Leviticus opens: [[the Lord called Moses and spoke to him from the tent of meeting >> Bible:Leviticus 1:1]]. God’s call leads into secrets. He is not summoned to sacrifice still in Egypt, but in the wilderness, at the tent of testimony. Whoever remains in Egypt’s vices cannot yet offer spiritual victims. Called Moses receives the law of offerings — not so the church may immolate Christ with bloody cattle, but so she may understand the [[rational burnt offering >> Bible:Romans 12:1]].

title: Hand upon the head of the victim
english: [[He shall lay his hand on the head of the offering, and it shall be acceptable >> Bible:Leviticus 1:4]]. The laid-on hand means communion: what we offer becomes ours in figure. Christ is the head; we the members. To lay the hand is to consent and to confess the sins that pass onto the victim. Blood is dashed at the altar, for [[without shedding of blood there is no forgiveness >> Bible:Hebrews 9:22]]. Our high priest, Christ, [[offered himself once >> Bible:Hebrews 7:27]].

title: The calf flayed and divided limb by limb
english: [[They shall flay the burnt offering and cut it limb from limb; Aaron’s sons put fire, wood, and the divided pieces on the altar >> Bible:Leviticus 1:6-9]]. The calf is Christ; stripping the hide of the letter opens the spiritual sense. To divide limb by limb is to order progress — fitting teaching to beginners, to those advancing, and to the perfect. Altar wood reaches to the wood of the passion; the fire from above is divinity. Inwards and feet washed with water announce the sacrament of baptism — [[who is clean needs only to wash the feet >> Bible:John 13:10]].

title: Offer your own proud flesh — Homilia I CLOSEOUT
english: Turn the figure to morals: you too have a [[calf >> Bible:Leviticus 1:3]] — proud flesh. If you would offer it to the Lord, bring it to the door of the tent — to the hearing of the divine books. Let the gift be male; lay on your hand and slaughter it before the Lord — the bridle of continence, as Paul: [[I pommel my body and subdue it >> Bible:1 Corinthians 9:27]]. Aaron’s sons in you — mind and sense — present the blood. Offer a [[living sacrifice, holy, pleasing to God; your rational worship >> Bible:Romans 12:1]]. Homilia I CLOSEOUT. Amen.
